needs.summary: Study for §7 done; the plan waits for approval. The React Aria base is `aria` (`--base aria`), and `components.json`'s style becomes `aria-nova`. All 16 installed ui components exist for it. AI Elements has no aria variant, `TooltipProvider` and `asChild` go away, and React Aria's collapsible keeps folded content mounted where Radix unmounted it. That last one needs a decision, and I propose one run. This step was denied the shadcn CLI, the Skill tool and node_modules, so the registry facts come from ui.shadcn.com's `aria-nova` registry (what `npx shadcn@latest` reads), react-aria's source and TanStack's docs. The implement step confirms them with the CLI first.
needs.needs:
This plan waits for your approval. Three questions:

1. **The base's name.** It is `aria`: the shadcn CLI's `--base aria` (base, radix or aria), shipped July 2026. `apps/web/components.json` goes from `"style": "radix-nova"` to `"style": "aria-nova"`. The style prefix is what the registry reads the base from. Approve?

2. **What won't exist on this base, and what I propose for each:**
   - **ui components.** All 16 installed ones exist in `aria-nova`: badge, bubble, button, card, collapsible, input, marker, message, message-scroller, separator, sheet, sidebar, skeleton, switch, tabs, tooltip. The base as a whole lacks `navigation-menu`, `menubar` and `form`; the app uses none of them.
   - **AI Elements** (`tool`, `reasoning`, `code-block`, `shimmer`). There is no React Aria variant (vercel/ai-elements#451 was still open when I read it). I propose adapting the four files by hand, each saying so in its header, as they already say their other changes.
   - **`TooltipProvider`.** It has no counterpart; each aria `TooltipTrigger` carries its own delay (0). I propose dropping it from `__root.tsx`.
   - **`asChild`.** It is gone. I propose `<Button asChild><Link/>` becomes `LinkButton`, and `<SidebarMenuButton asChild><Link/>` becomes the menu button given `href`. Both go through TanStack's `createLink`, so `to` stays typed and hover preloading (`defaultPreload: 'intent'`) is kept.
   - **`@radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state`** (used in `reasoning.tsx`). I propose local state, the way `SidebarProvider` already does it, then removing it and `radix-ui` from `package.json`.
   - **The switch.** React Aria's switch is itself a `<label>`. I propose the aria example's pattern: a sibling `<label htmlFor>` in place of the Factory's wrapping label.
   - **Folded content (this one needs your choice).** Radix's collapsible unmounts content while folded; React Aria's `DisclosurePanel` keeps it mounted and only hidden (checked in its source).
     - **(A) Proposed:** the conversation's folds (a tool call, a fold of calls, a thought) mount their content only while open, as today. Nothing extra is rendered or highlighted by shiki on page load for every folded call. The unit tests and e2e checks that folded content is not drawn stay as they are. Costs: find-in-page doesn't reach folded text, and the closing animation is lost.
     - **(B)** Keep React Aria's hidden panels. Find-in-page reveals and opens folded text. Costs: every folded call's input and output is rendered and highlighted on load, and `components.test.ts:401,416` and `run.ts:1090,1097` change from "not in the markup" to "hidden".

3. **One run or parts.** I propose one run. About 28 files, 16 of them re-added by the CLI; the hand-written part is 8 app files and one test file. Parts don't split cleanly. `Button` is imported by sheet, sidebar and message-scroller, and every caller moves from `onClick` to `onPress`, so a first part would carry most of the switch. Between parts, both libraries would ship and each part would pay a build and an e2e run.

Also, for whoever approves:
- This step's `npx shadcn` and reads of `node_modules` were denied, and `.claude/settings.json` does not allow `npx shadcn@latest`. An implement step in `dontAsk` mode would be denied the CLI too.
- The pinned shadcn skill's base rules name only `radix` and `base`. Refreshing it is not in this plan.

needs.summary: Planned `Engine.say` / `ae say` and the `said` event. From Claude Code's docs, a process can reach a running `--bg` session: every session listens on a per-session Unix inbox socket, the same channel `SendMessage` uses on one machine. Stop-and-resume would also work, so per the brief I'm blocking for a person to pick a reading. The plan below is for my recommendation, delivery over that socket, and it starts with a probe because the docs don't say where the socket is registered or what a message line looks like.
needs.needs:
Pick how `say` reaches a running `claude --bg` session. It waits for your answer, given with `wf retry`.

A. Post to the session's own inbox socket (recommended; the plan below). Claude Code's docs (cross-session-messaging, "The session's inbox socket") say every session, `--bg` and `-p` included, binds a Unix socket that only this OS user can open. A message there is read between tool calls, so a running tool is never cut off, or it starts a new turn if the session is idle. A sender that doesn't claim a permission class reaches sessions in `auto`, `acceptEdits`, `dontAsk` or manual mode, and is held for approval in `bypassPermissions`. Costs: nothing to spend, the text arrives verbatim, and it takes milliseconds. But the docs never say where a session registers its socket on disk ("each session registers itself in files on disk") or what a message line looks like after the optional auth line. Step 1 has to find both on this machine's Claude Code before any code is written. The engine would then depend on internals that a release can change without warning, and only `AE_LIVE=1` would catch that.

A2. Relay through a short `claude -p` session that has only `SendMessage` and addresses `ae/<task>/<n>` by name. Every part of this is documented. Costs: one model turn per `say` (haiku-sized, a few seconds) and a second transcript on disk. Also, the docs say "Claude writes the actual message itself": what arrives can differ from what was journalled, which weakens the trace this feature exists for.

B. Stop and resume: `claude stop`, then `claude --bg --resume <id> "<text>"` as the next attempt. Verbatim and documented. Costs: it kills the turn in flight. The engine settles a stopped attempt as `stopped`, so B needs either `decide` to read the `said` event (the brief forbids that) or a new per-attempt prompt field on `starting`/`SpawnRequest`. And it repeats what `wf retry --message` already does for a step.

C. Journal only: `say` writes `said` and delivers nothing; the person sends the message by hand. No risk, but the record then holds a claim, not a delivery.

Considered and dropped: channels (`--dangerously-load-development-channels`). They're a research preview, need an engine-owned MCP server on every spawn, and open a start-up confirmation dialog that a `--bg` session with no terminal can't answer. Codex has no channel in any reading: `codex exec` reads its prompt once, so it's refused in its own words.

If you choose A and step 1 can't find the socket's registration file or a message line Claude Code delivers, the implementing step signs off blocked with what it found instead of guessing.

needs.summary: The study is done. I recommend react-markdown 10.1.0 with remark-gfm 4.0.1, replacing `streamdown`. The web app already has `streamdown`, and §5 says it has no renderer: today it renders the conversation with raw HTML turned on (sanitized) and code blocks not highlighted. The build plan below is for react-markdown; the run waits for the operator to approve the renderer (or name another) and settle two smaller readings.
needs.needs:
This waits for your approval of the plan. Pick the renderer (approve the recommendation or name another) and settle the two readings at the end. The table and sources are below.

**A finding first.** §5 says `apps/web` has no markdown renderer. It has one: `streamdown` 2.6.0 (`apps/web/package.json:29`), added in 5c30c9c on 2026-09-13.
- **Where it runs:** every said turn, the closeout summary and each thought on the session page and in the Activity tab (`ai-elements/response.tsx:14`, `ai-elements/reasoning.tsx:176`, `conversation/Turns.tsx:27,37,180`).
- **Raw HTML is on.** `Response` sets no plugins, so streamdown's defaults apply: `rehype-raw`, then `rehype-sanitize`, then `rehype-harden`. An agent's raw HTML is rendered as HTML (sanitized), not shown as text [10a, 10b].
- **No highlighting.** `@streamdown/code` is not in `package-lock.json`, so code blocks render as plain text [10d].

**Recommendation: react-markdown 10.1.0 with remark-gfm 4.0.1, replacing streamdown.**

Why:
- **Safe as it ships.** It is the only candidate whose shipped settings already meet §5. Raw HTML becomes a text node, and a link whose protocol is not http(s), irc(s), mailto or xmpp gets an empty href [2]. No sanitizer is needed, and it renders React elements, not an HTML string [1].
- **Uses the existing shiki component.** It is the only one that renders code blocks through `CodeBlock` as a React component, with no HTML string: `components.pre` renders it, and the component highlights asynchronously in its own effect.
- **All five GFM features:** tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolink literals and footnotes [6].
- **Mostly installed already.** Its pipeline is in the lockfile through streamdown: remark-parse, remark-rehype, remark-gfm, unified and hast-util-to-jsx-runtime (`package-lock.json:9793-9814`).
- **Smaller.** Taking out streamdown removes a 147.6 kB package [11] and its HTML-rendering default from the conversation.

What it costs against the others:
- **Size.** About 44 kB gzipped by bundlephobia's count, against about 24 kB for marked plus DOMPurify [11]. It also lands in the run page's chunk, where today markdown is only in the lazy conversation chunk.
- **Dependencies.** Two new ones (react-markdown, remark-gfm), less streamdown: one more than today.
- **Release pace.** Its last release is 18 months old (10.1.0, 2025-03-07); marked released on 2026-09-12 and markdown-it on 2026-09-11 [5, 8d, 9c].
- **Parsing.** It parses on each render, so the component is memoized on its text.
- **No typography plugin.** Headings, lists and tables are styled by hand.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Raw HTML as it ships | Shown as text (`raw` becomes a text node); `skipHtml` drops it [2] | `html: false`, so it is escaped [8a] | Passed through: "Marked does not sanitize the output HTML" [9a] | Encoded unless `allowDangerousHtml` [7] | Rendered by rehype-raw, then sanitized [10a, 10b] |
| Links as it ships | Other protocols get an empty href [2] | `validateLink` blocks `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` and most `data:` [8a] | Nothing blocked | Blocked unless `allowDangerousProtocol` [7] | rehype-harden allows `*`; the sanitize schema allows http(s), irc(s), mailto, xmpp and tel; a link-safety modal is on by default [10a, 10b] |
| With a sanitizer | Not needed | Not needed with `html: false` | DOMPurify is required (+10.7 kB gzipped) [9a, 11] | Not needed | Already has one |

**Why not the others:**
- **marked:** it renders raw HTML, so it needs DOMPurify, and it produces a string, so shiki cannot go through the component.
- **markdown-it:** safe by default, but a string too; its `highlight` hook is synchronous, and task lists and footnotes need plugins.
- **micromark / mdast used directly:** the same safety as react-markdown, but four or five direct dependencies and glue code we would own.
- **Keeping streamdown:** no new dependency, but to meet §5 we would override its rehype plugins, turn off its link modal, and add `@streamdown/code` or an undocumented `code` override. That is fighting four defaults of a 147.6 kB package whose main feature this board does not use.
- **Sharing with the CLI:** nothing. `wf decide` stays plain, and I did not look into terminal renderers.

**Two readings I took (tell me if either is wrong):**
1. **"A step's body on the Workflows page and the step's page."** I read it as a new step page, `/workflows/<repo|yours>/<workflow>/<step>`, opened from the step's block and from a list of step links under the graph. That page renders the body. The Workflows card stays a graph, and the run page's step section renders its body too. The other reading lists every body inline on each Workflows card: a longer page, but the same component.
2. **"A blocked step's needs."** Rendered in closeouts, the run page's step section, the conversation and the Decide answer rows (a scrolling box replaces the 4-line clamp). The banner at the top of a run's page and the Factory's cards and nodes keep their plain one-line `asks: …`, since a rendered plan there would push everything down. The other reading renders the banner too.
